cards.title: Attempt on Extended states for the three-dimensional Anderson model at weak disorder
cards.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Review the failure of perturbation theory and test a restricted version on a tree-like subgraph. Result: On the Bethe lattice a.c. spectrum is known (Klein; Aizenman-Warzel) because the self-consistent equation for the Green function has a stable solution; on Z^3 the corresponding equation is not closed. A known partial statement is that the disorder-averaged Green function has diffusive behaviour up to times lambda^{-2-delta} (Erdos-Salmhofer-Yau), which is the kinetic regime and does not reach the infinite-time statement. I tested the possibility of transferring the tree result through a spanning tree of Z^3: the operator restricted to a spanning tree is not the operator on Z^3, and removing the edges changes the spectrum non-perturbatively, so no transfer. No result; the problem is recorded as attempted with the explicit obstruction that the only tools proving a.c. spectrum are tree-specific. Obstruction: Absence of a closed self-consistency equation on Z^3; kinetic-regime results stop at finite times.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0056-extended-states-for-the-three-dimensional-anderson-model-at-weak-disor
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

cards.title: Open problem: Extended states for the three-dimensional Anderson model at weak disorder
cards.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Prove existence of absolutely continuous spectrum (delocalised states) for the random Schrodinger operator -Delta + lambda V on Z^3 at small disorder lambda, and GOE local statistics for its finite-volume restriction. Source: Bourgade: Random band matrices, ICM 2018 survey, Section 2.1, p. 7.

cards.title: Constructible universe
cards.body: In set theory, the constructible universe, denoted by is a particular class of sets that can be described entirely in terms of simpler sets. is the union of the constructible hierarchy . It was introduced by Kurt Gödel in 1938, who proved that the constructible universe is an inner model of ZF set theory, and also that the axiom of choice and the generalized continuum hypothesis are true in the constructible universe. This shows that both propositions are consistent with the basic axioms of set theory, if ZF itself is consistent. Since many other theorems only hold in systems in which one or both of the propositions is true, their consistency is an important result.

cards.title: Approximate Identity (Good Kernels)
cards.body:
A family $(K_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ in $L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ (or a sequence $K_N$ with $N\to\infty$; the same definition works on $\mathbb T$) is an approximate identity if (i) $\int K_\varepsilon=1$ for every $\varepsilon$; (ii) $\sup_\varepsilon\|K_\varepsilon\|_1<\infty$; (iii) for every $\delta>0$, $\int_{|x|\ge\delta}|K_\varepsilon(x)|\,dx\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. If $K\in L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\int K=1$, the dilates $K_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-d}K(x/\varepsilon)$ form an approximate identity. Standard examples: the Gauss-Weierstrass (heat) kernel $\varepsilon^{-d}e^{-\pi|x|^2/\varepsilon^2}$, the Poisson kernel of the half-space, the Fejer kernel $F_N$ and the Poisson kernel $P_r(x)=\sum_n r^{|n|}e^{2\pi i n x}$ ($r\uparrow1$) on $\mathbb T$. Non-example: the Dirichlet kernel $D_N$ satisfies (i) but not (ii), since $\|D_N\|_1\to\infty$; this is the root of the divergence phenomena for Fourier series. Some texts add the stronger condition $\sup_{|x|\ge\delta}|K_\varepsilon(x)|\to0$, which is the convenient hypothesis for convergence at a point of continuity of a merely integrable $f$ (the tail is then controlled by $\|f\|_1$). Almost-everywhere convergence at Lebesgue points needs more than either condition: the usual hypothesis is the dilation structure $K_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-d}K(x/\varepsilon)$ together with an integrable radially nonincreasing majorant of $|K|$.
each K_eps is Lebesgue integrable

cards.title: Weyl's Lemma
cards.body:
Let Omega in R^n be open and u in L^1_loc(Omega) satisfy integral_Omega u (Laplacian of phi) dx = 0 for every phi in C_c^infinity(Omega). Then u agrees almost everywhere with a function that is harmonic, hence real-analytic, in Omega. More generally, if P is a linear differential operator with smooth coefficients that is elliptic (nonvanishing principal symbol), then every distributional solution of Pu = f with f smooth is smooth; ellipticity, not any a priori regularity of u, is what does the work.
Omega open in R^n
u in L^1_loc(Omega)
integral u times Laplacian of phi vanishes for all phi in C_c^infinity(Omega) (u is harmonic in the sense of distributions)

cards.title: L^p-L^q Duality, and Exactly Where sigma-Finiteness Is Needed
cards.body:
Let (Omega, F, mu) be a measure space and 1 <= p < infinity with conjugate exponent q = p/(p-1) (q = infinity when p = 1). For 1 < p < infinity the map g -> (f -> integral f g dmu) is an isometric isomorphism from L^q(mu) onto the dual space L^p(mu)^*, for ANY measure space. For p = 1 the same map from L^infinity(mu) onto L^1(mu)^* is an isometric isomorphism provided mu is sigma-finite (or, more generally, localizable); without such a hypothesis it can fail to be surjective. The dual of L^infinity is strictly larger than L^1 whenever L^infinity is infinite-dimensional: on ([0,1], Lebesgue) a Banach limit or a Hahn-Banach extension of the functional f -> lim_{x -> 0} f(x) from C[0,1] gives an element of (L^infinity)^* not represented by any L^1 function. So the duality chain (L^1)^* = L^infinity does NOT continue to (L^infinity)^* = L^1, and L^1 is not reflexive; L^p is reflexive exactly for 1 < p < infinity. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 6.15]
1 <= p < infinity
for p = 1: mu sigma-finite (or localizable)
no hypothesis on mu for 1 < p < infinity

cards.title: Lebesgue decomposition into absolutely continuous and singular parts
cards.body:
Let (X, M) be a measurable space and let mu and nu be SIGMA-FINITE positive measures on M. Then nu can be written as nu = nu_a + nu_s with nu_a absolutely continuous with respect to mu (nu_a << mu) and nu_s mutually singular with mu (nu_s perp mu), and this decomposition is unique. Combined with the Radon-Nikodym theorem, nu_a has a density: there is an M-measurable f >= 0, unique up to mu-null sets, with nu_a(E) = integral_E f dmu for all E in M; f is in L^1(mu) exactly when nu_a is a finite measure. The statement extends to nu a signed or complex measure of finite total variation with mu sigma-finite. WHERE IT FAILS: (a) sigma-finiteness of nu is essential for existence of the decomposition. Take X = [0,1] with the Borel sets, mu = Lebesgue measure and nu = counting measure. If nu = nu_a + nu_s with nu_a << mu and nu_s perp mu, pick E with mu(E) = 0 and nu_s(X minus E) = 0. For any x outside E we get nu({x}) = nu_a({x}), and mu({x}) = 0 forces nu_a({x}) = 0, contradicting nu({x}) = 1. So X minus E is empty, i.e. E = X, contradicting mu(X) = 1 > 0. (b) sigma-finiteness of mu is essential for the DENSITY. With mu = counting measure on [0,1] and nu = Lebesgue measure one has nu << mu, yet no f satisfies nu(E) = integral_E f dmu (evaluating on singletons forces f = 0). The decomposition itself survives here (nu_s = 0), but the Radon-Nikodym half does not. (c) Uniqueness is uniqueness of the pair of measures; the density f is only mu-almost everywhere unique.
(X, M) is a measurable space
mu is sigma-finite (needed for the Radon-Nikodym density)
nu is sigma-finite (needed for existence of the decomposition); for signed or complex nu, finite total variation
absolute continuity and mutual singularity are with respect to the same sigma-algebra M

cards.title: Radon-Nikodym theorem
cards.body: Radon-Nikodym theorem: if mu and nu are sigma-finite measures on the same measurable space and nu is absolutely continuous with respect to mu (mu-null sets are nu-null), then there is a nonnegative measurable density f, unique up to mu-null sets, with nu(A) equal to the integral of f over A against mu for every measurable A; f is the Radon-Nikodym derivative dnu/dmu. Sigma-finiteness cannot be dropped (Lebesgue measure against counting measure on R fails).
